versions.short: The bill would direct the Secretary of the Interior to carry out a feasibility study on ways to reduce invasive species flowing downstream from Glen Canyon Dam, including options such as a thermal curtain or a selective water withdrawal system. If an option is found feasible under federal reclamation law, the Secretary could begin designing and building it. The Secretary would have to finish the study within 18 months of enactment, prepare a summary report covering the alternatives, costs, and effects on hydropower, and send that report to the relevant congressional committees within 90 days after completing it. The study would be paid for with appropriated federal funds, and the authority would expire five years after enactment.
